speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me your age and describe when these skin lesions first appeared? Are they itchy, painful, or changing in appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions fluid-filled vesicles or do they appear as firm, raised papules with a central dimple? I will also inspect the distribution of the rash to see if it is concentrated on the trunk or spread to the face and extremities. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the classic presentation of pearly, umbilicated papules and the daycare exposure history, this is highly suggestive of molluscum contagiosum.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
